chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from al-'Ala', from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them), who said:
I asked him about a man who performed Zihar from his wife five times or more, so he said: Ali (peace be said: Ali (peace be upon him) said: 'For each time, there is an expiation.'
He said: And I asked him about a man who performed Zihar from his wife, then divorced her before he copulated with her; is there an expiation? He said: 'No.'

He said: And I asked him about Zihar upon the free woman and the slave woman, so he said: 'Yes.' It was said: 'If he performed Zihar in Sha'ban and did not find what he could emancipate?' He said: 'He should wait until he fasts the month of Ramadan, then he should fast two consecutive months.'
And if he performed Zihar while he was a traveler, he should wait until he returns. If he fasts and attains wealth, let him fulfill that which he had begun with.

key_terms.الْحُرَّة: Al-Hurrah: A free woman (as opposed to a slave woman).
key_terms.رَمَضَانَ: Ramadan: The ninth month of the Islamic lunar calendar, known for fasting.
key_terms.شَعْبَانَ: Sha'ban: The eighth month of the Islamic lunar calendar.
key_terms.ظَهَار: Zihar: A form of divorce in Islamic law where a man declares his wife's back to be like his mother's back, prohibiting sexual relations until expiation is made.
key_terms.كَفَّارَةٌ: Kaffarah: Expiation or atonement for a specific act or sin.
key_terms.مُسَافِرٌ: Musafir: A traveler, who may have different rulings regarding prayer and fasting.

ai.seo_question: What is the expiation for Zihar in Shia jurisprudence and how does it apply to travelers?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi elucidates the jurisprudential nuances of Zihar, establishing that each declaration incurs a distinct expiation (Kaffarah) and clarifying that divorce prior to consummation exempts the husband from this penalty. It further details the procedural flexibility for travelers and those with delayed means, emphasizing the continuity of the initial obligation once resources become available. This ruling reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on the individualized nature of the penalty and the practical accommodation of human circumstances within the divine law.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Al A’ala, from Muhammad Bin Muslim, (It has been narrated) from one of the two (5th or 6th Imamasws), said, ‘I asked himasws about a man who did Zahaar from his wife five times, or more. So heasws said: ‘Aliasws said: ‘In place of each time, is an expiation’.
He (the narrator) said, ‘And I asked himasws about a man who did Zahaar from his wife, then divorced her before he copulated with her, does an expiation occur upon him?’ Heasws said: ‘No’.

He (the narrator) said, ‘And I asked himasws about the Zahaar upon the free woman and the slave woman. So heasws said: ‘Yes’. It was said, ‘Supposing if he did Zahaar in Shaban and did not find what he could emancipate?’ Heasws said:’ He should wait until he Fasts the Month of Ramazaan, then he should Fast for two months consecutively.
And if he had done Zahaar and he is a traveller, he should wait until he returns home. So if he Fasts and attains wealth, so let him fulfill that which he had begun with’.
en.sarwar: 12. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn al-Hakam from al-‘Ala’ from Muhammad ibn Muslim who has said the following:

“I once asked one of the two Imam, (abu Ja‘far or abu ‘Abd Allah), ‘Alayhim al-Salam, about the case of a man who forms al-Zihar about his wife five times or more. He (the Imam) said, Tor every time there is expiation.’

He (the narrator) has said, ‘I asked him (the Imam) about a man who forms al- Zihar about his wife, then divorces her before going to bed with her; if there is expiation on him. He (the Imam) said, ‘No, there is no expiation on him.’

He (the narrator) has said, ‘I asked him (the Imam) about al-Zihar of free and a slave-girl. He (the Imam) said, ‘Yes, it can happen.’ It was asked, ‘If it takes place in the month of Sha’ban and he cannot find a slave to free.’ He (the Imam) said, ‘He must wait until he completes fasting of the month of Ramadan, then fast for two consecutive months;
and if he forms al-Zihar on a journey he must wait until he comes home. If he fasts then finds assets, he continues with what he has started.’”
